metadata.title: On a thin film model with insoluble surfactant

extraction_notes.note: The three itemised Wiener-space inequalities (4)-(6) are named in the text ('Poincare-like inequality', 'algebra property', 'interpolation inequality'), so each item is an external standard theorem that contains its numbered equation. They could instead have been left as bare equation nodes.

The proofs of Theorems 1 and 2 are prose that runs over whole sections. Each section or subsection is one proof node, and the existence, decay and uniqueness parts of each theorem are nested claims. Following the continuation rule, the subsection parts point uses-edges to the section outline. Separate uses-edges record that the a priori estimates feed the other parts.

The labels eq:system, eq:systemA and eq:systemlinearized sit on subequations groups that have no fact id, so the finishing step could not resolve their \eqref uses-edges; I added them by hand (conf 0.9). Section 4.3 cites \eqref{delta}, which is Theorem 2's rate, where the S=0 rate (delta2) is meant, and (34) uses an undefined $\gamma$. Both are kept as written.
The sentence that introduces $f_0,\Theta_0$ also displays the whole perturbation system (10), so the equation node EP10 is nested inside the definition DP10.
Remark 2 is in effect a worked example of Theorem 1, with explicit constants. It stays a remark because it sits in a remark environment.

Literature mentions in the introduction that state no result (Renardy's local existence 'has been studied', traveling waves) and the acknowledgements get no node. The intro's assumption $\sigma(s)=1-s$ is restated at the start of Section 3.1, and that repeat gets no node either.

nodes.name: Jensen-Grotberg thin film system with insoluble surfactant
nodes.statement: {2} \partial_t h &=-\partial_x \left[ \frac{h^2}{2}\partial_x \sigma(\Gamma)-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h^3\partial_x h + \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h^3\partial_x^3h+\mathcal{A}\frac{\partial_x h}{h} \right]\; && \mbox{in}\quad \Omega_T\\ \partial_t \Gamma &=- \partial_x \left[\Gamma \left(h \partial_x \sigma(\Gamma)-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2} h^2 \partial_x h +\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2} h^2 \partial_x^3 h + \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2} \frac{\partial_x h }{h^{2}}\right)-\mathcal{D}\partial_x \Gamma \right]\;\qquad&& \mbox{in}\quad \Omega_T.
nodes.statement_short: Coupled evolution equations for film height $h$ and surfactant concentration $\Gamma$ (lubrication approximation).

nodes.name: Time-space domain $\Omega_T$
nodes.statement: Here, $\Omega_T:=(0,T)\times \Omega$ denotes the time-space domain for the unknown functions $h$ and $\Gamma$, with $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}$ being an open, bounded interval.

nodes.name: Initial and boundary conditions for the thin film system
nodes.statement: The system \eqref{eq:system} is supplemented with initial conditions \[ h(0,x)=h_0(x)\quad \mbox{and}\quad \Gamma(0,x)=\Gamma_0(x)\qquad \mbox{for all} \quad x\in \Omega, \] where $h_0$ and $\Gamma_0$ are given functions and boundary conditions $$ \partial_x h =\partial_x \Gamma=0, \quad \mathcal{S}\partial_x^3 f =0 \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad x\in \partial \Omega. $$
nodes.statement_short: Initial data $h_0,\Gamma_0$ and Neumann-type boundary conditions on $\partial\Omega$.

nodes.name: Model parameters G, S, A, D
nodes.statement: The appearing parameters represent a modified gravitational constant ($\mathcal{G}$), surface tension coefficient ($\mathcal{S}$), Hamaker constant ($\mathcal{A}$), which corresponds to the effects of van der Waals forces, and surface diffusion coefficient ($\mathcal{D}$).

nodes.name: Surface tension equation of state $\sigma$
nodes.statement: Moreover, $\sigma$ is the constitutive equation of state relating the surface tension to the surfactant concentration.

nodes.name: Surface tension positive and nonincreasing
nodes.statement: As the presence of surfactant reduces surface tension, $\sigma$ is assumed to be positive and nonincreasing.

nodes.name: Equation of state $\sigma_\beta$
nodes.statement: A commonly used description for the dependence of the surface tension on the surfactant is given by (cf. \cite{sheludko1967thin,BG,GG}) \[ \sigma_\beta (s):= (\beta +1) \left[1-s+\left(\frac{\beta +1}{\beta}\right)^\frac{1}{3}s\right]^{-3}-\beta, \qquad s\in[0,1] \] for $\beta \in (0,\infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: One-parameter family of surface-tension laws $\sigma_\beta(s)$ on $[0,1]$.

nodes.name: Linear equation of state $\sigma(s)=1-s$
nodes.statement: For simplicity reasons, in the present work, we assume that $\sigma$ is given by the limit for $\beta\to \infty$ in $\sigma_\beta$, that is $$ \sigma (s)= 1-s, \qquad s\in[0,1]. $$
nodes.statement_short: Take the $\beta\to\infty$ limit: $\sigma(s)=1-s$.

nodes.name: Critical micelle concentration
nodes.statement: Let us mention that the scaling Jensen and Grotberg used for the surfactant concentration is given by \[ \Gamma(t,x)\mapsto \Gamma_m^{-1} \Gamma( t, x), \] where $\Gamma_m>0$ is the so-called \emph{critical micelle concentration}.

nodes.name: Initial surfactant concentration bounded by 1
nodes.statement: Consequently, it is natural to assume that the initial surfactant concentration $\Gamma_0$ satisfies $0\leq \Gamma_0\leq 1$.

nodes.name: Local well-posedness and exponential stability for soluble surfactant (EHLW)
nodes.statement: Moreover, they proved local well-posedness in the space of square integrable functions $L^2$ by means of semigroup theory as well as asymptotic stability with exponential decay of the equilibrium. We would like to emphasize that their stability result is stated for positive initial data in the $L^2$-based Sobolev space $H^2$. The result shows in particular, that starting with $H^2$ data close to the flat steady state there exists a unique global strong solution.
nodes.statement_short: Local $L^2$ well-posedness via semigroups and exponential stability of the flat state for positive $H^2$ data.

nodes.name: Bruell's result for two-phase thin film with insoluble surfactant
nodes.statement: A similar result for a two-phase thin film equation with insoluble surfactant was shown by Bruell \cite{B1} for the gravity ($\mathcal S =\mathcal A=0$) as well as for the capillary driven film ($\mathcal G=\mathcal A=0$).

nodes.name: Global weak solutions for thin film with insoluble surfactant (EHLW, Bruell)
nodes.statement: The existence of nonnegative global weak solutions for the thin film equation with insoluble surfactant was proved by Escher, Hillairet, Lauren{\c{c}}ot \& Walker \cite{EHLW11} for the gravity driven thin film ($\mathcal S=\mathcal A=0$), and \cite{EHLW4th} for the corresponding capillary driven film ($\mathcal G=\mathcal A=0$) and by Bruell \cite{B2} for the two-phase thin film equation with insoluble surfactant under the influence of capillary forces (see also \cite{GW06, CT13}).

nodes.name: Torus $\mathbb T$
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbb T}:=[-\pi,\pi)$.

nodes.name: Sobolev spaces $W^{n,p}(\mathbb T)$
nodes.statement: W^{n,p}({\mathbb T})=\left\{u\in L^p({\mathbb T})\text{ such that } \|u\|_{W^{n,p}({\mathbb T})}^p:= \|u\|_{L^p}^p+\|\partial_x^n u\|_{L^p}^p<\infty \right\}
nodes.label: Sobinhomo2

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients and Fourier series
nodes.statement: We recall the expression of the $k-$th Fourier coefficient and the Fourier series of a $2\pi-$periodic integrable function $u$, $$ \hat{u}(k)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{{\mathbb T}}u(x)e^{-ix k}dx,\;u(x)=\sum_{k\in{\mathbb Z}}\hat{u}(k)e^{ix k}. $$

nodes.name: Wiener spaces $\dot A^s(\mathbb T)$
nodes.statement: \dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})=\left\{u\in L^1({\mathbb T})\text{ such that } \|u\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}:=\sum_{k\in{\mathbb Z}} |k|^s|\hat{u}(k)| < \infty\right\}.
nodes.statement_short: $\dot A^s$: functions whose Fourier coefficients weighted by $|k|^s$ are absolutely summable.
nodes.label: Wienerinhomo

nodes.name: Wiener algebra is a Banach algebra; Banach scale
nodes.statement: We note that $\dot{A}^0({\mathbb T})=A({\mathbb T})$ is a Banach algebra and $\{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})\mid s\geq 0\}$ form a Banach scale.
conclusions: $\dot{A}^0({\mathbb T})=A({\mathbb T})$ is a Banach algebra
$\{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})\mid s\geq 0\}$ form a Banach scale

nodes.name: Poincare-like inequality in Wiener spaces
nodes.statement: Let $p\geq q\geq 0$, then \begin{equation} \|f\|_{ \dot A^q }\leq \|f\|_{ \dot A^p} \text{ for all } f\in \dot A^p({\mathbb T}). \end{equation}
conclusions: \|f\|_{ \dot A^q }\leq \|f\|_{ \dot A^p} \text{ for all } f\in  \dot A^p({\mathbb T}).
nodes.statement_short: Wiener norms are monotone in the regularity index: $\|f\|_{\dot A^q}\le\|f\|_{\dot A^p}$ for $p\ge q$.

nodes.name: Poincare-like inequality (4)
nodes.statement: \|f\|_{ \dot A^q }\leq \|f\|_{ \dot A^p} \text{ for all } f\in \dot A^p({\mathbb T}).
nodes.label: lem:P

nodes.name: Algebra inequality in Wiener spaces
nodes.statement: Let $s\in \{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ be a fixed parameter and $f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T})$, then, due to the convexity of $x^s$ in this range, \begin{equation} \|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2^{s-1}\left\|f\|_{\dot A^s}\|g\|_{\dot A^0}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|g\|_{\dot A^s}\right)\leq 2^{s}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s}\|g\|_{\dot{A}^s}, \end{equation} while, as a consequence of subadditivity of $x^s$, for $s\in (0,1)$, we have \[ \|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2\|f\|_{\dot A^s}\|g\|_{\dot A^s}. \]
assumptions: $s\in \{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ be a fixed parameter and $f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T})$
conclusions: \|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2\|f\|_{\dot A^s}\|g\|_{\dot A^s}.
nodes.statement_short: Product estimate in $\dot A^s$: $\|fg\|_{\dot A^s}\le 2^s\|f\|_{\dot A^s}\|g\|_{\dot A^s}$ (constant 2 for $s\in(0,1)$).

nodes.name: Interpolation inequality in Wiener spaces
nodes.statement: Due to the H\"older inequality, we have the following interpolation inequality \begin{equation} \|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s}}^{\theta}\quad \mbox{for all }\quad 0<\theta<1. \end{equation}
conclusions: \|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s}}^{\theta}

nodes.name: Interpolation inequality (6)
nodes.statement: \|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s}}^{\theta}\quad \mbox{for all }\quad 0<\theta<1.
nodes.label: interpolation

nodes.name: Thin film system with linear equation of state
nodes.statement: {2} \partial_t h &=-\partial_x \left[ -\frac{h^2}{2}\partial_x\Gamma-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h^3\partial_x h + \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h^3\partial_x^3h+\mathcal{A}\frac{\partial_x h}{h} \right],\; &&\mbox{in}\quad \Omega_T \\ \partial_t \Gamma &=- \partial_x \left[\Gamma \left(-h \partial_x \Gamma-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2} h^2 \partial_x h +\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2} h^2 \partial_x^3 h + \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2} \frac{\partial_x h }{h^{2}}\right)-\mathcal{D}\partial_x \Gamma \right],\;&&\mbox{in}\quad \Omega_T,
nodes.statement_short: System (1) with $\sigma(s)=1-s$.

nodes.name: No-flux boundary conditions
nodes.statement: \partial_x h =\partial_x \Gamma=0, \quad \mathcal{S}\partial_x^3 f =0 \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad x\in \partial \Omega.
nodes.label: eq:boundary

nodes.name: Equivalence of the periodic formulation with the interval problem
nodes.statement: If $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ are the initial data on an interval $\overline \Omega=[0,L]$ satisfying the boundary conditions \eqref{eq:boundary}, we set \[ \bar h_0(x):= h_0(|x|) ,\quad \bar \Gamma_0(x):=\Gamma_0(|x|)\qquad \mbox{for}\quad x\in [-L,L]. \] In view of the symmetry of \eqref{eq:systemA}, the evenness of initial data is preserved and any solution of \eqref{eq:systemA} on $[0,L]$ with initial data $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ satisfying the boundary conditions \eqref{eq:boundary}, can be identified with the corresponding solution to even initial data $(\bar h_0, \bar \Gamma_0)$ on the periodic cell $[-L,L]$ restricted to the half-domain $[0,L]$.
nodes.statement_short: Even extension to $[-L,L]$ turns the Neumann interval problem into an equivalent periodic problem.
assumptions: $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ are the initial data on an interval $\overline \Omega=[0,L]$ satisfying the boundary conditions \eqref{eq:boundary}
conclusions: the evenness of initial data is preserved

nodes.name: Proof of conservation of mass
nodes.statement: It follows immediately from the structure of the equations \eqref{eq:systemA} that the initial mass is preserved in time:
nodes.statement_short: Direct: both equations are in divergence form, so spatial integrals are conserved.

nodes.name: Conservation of mass
nodes.statement: Let $(h,\Gamma)$ be a solution of \eqref{eq:systemA} on a time interval $[0,T)$, then \[ \int_{{\mathbb T}} h(t,x)\,dx = \int_{{\mathbb T}} h_0(x)\,dx\quad\mbox{and}\quad \int_{{\mathbb T}} \Gamma(t,x)\,dx = \int_{{\mathbb T}} \Gamma_0(x)\,dx\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T). \]
assumptions: Let $(h,\Gamma)$ be a solution of \eqref{eq:systemA} on a time interval $[0,T)$
conclusions: \int_{{\mathbb T}} h(t,x)\,dx = \int_{{\mathbb T}} h_0(x)\,dx\quad\mbox{and}\quad \int_{{\mathbb T}} \Gamma(t,x)\,dx = \int_{{\mathbb T}} \Gamma_0(x)\,dx\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T).

nodes.name: Mean values $h_\sharp$, $\Gamma_\sharp$
nodes.statement: If $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ are nonnegative bounded initial data, we set $$ h_\sharp=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb T} h_0(x)dx\quad\mbox{and}\quad \Gamma_\sharp=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb T} \Gamma_0(x)dx. $$

nodes.name: Mean values form a steady state
nodes.statement: The constants $h_\sharp$ and $\Gamma_\sharp$ represent the mean of the initial data and they are a steady state of the system \eqref{eq:systemA}.
conclusions: they are a steady state of the system \eqref{eq:systemA}

nodes.name: Deviation unknowns $f$, $\Theta$
nodes.statement: f=h-h_\sharp,\quad \Theta=\Gamma-\Gamma_\sharp,
nodes.label: newunknown

nodes.name: Perturbation system and initial displacements $f_0$, $\Theta_0$
nodes.statement: In the new variables \eqref{newunknown}, the system \eqref{eq:systemA} can be rewritten as \begin{subequations} \begin{alignat}{2} \partial_t f-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\partial_x^2 \Theta +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\partial_x^2 f+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\partial_x^4 f&=\sum_{j=1}^4 N_j,\; &&\mbox{in}\quad (0,T)\times {\mathbb T}\\ \partial_t \Theta -\left(h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\partial_x^2\Theta+\left(\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\right) \partial_x^2f+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2 \partial_x^4f &= \sum_{j=5}^8 N_j,\;&& \mbox{in}\quad (0,T)\times {\mathbb T} \end{alignat} \end{subequations} with initial conditions \[ f(0,x)=f_0(x)\quad \mbox{and}\quad \Theta(0,x)=\Theta_0(x)\qquad \mbox{for all} \quad x\in \Omega, \] where $f_0(x)=h_0(x)-h_\sharp$ and $\Theta_0(x)=\Gamma_0(x)-\Gamma_\sharp$ are the initial displacement functions from the flat states $h_\sharp$ and $\Gamma_\sharp$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrites the system for $f,\Theta$ as linear part plus nonlinearities $N_j$, with initial displacements $f_0,\Theta_0$.

nodes.name: Perturbation system for $(f,\Theta)$
nodes.statement: {2} \partial_t f-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\partial_x^2 \Theta +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\partial_x^2 f+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\partial_x^4 f&=\sum_{j=1}^4 N_j,\; &&\mbox{in}\quad (0,T)\times {\mathbb T}\\ \partial_t \Theta -\left(h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\partial_x^2\Theta+\left(\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\right) \partial_x^2f+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2 \partial_x^4f &= \sum_{j=5}^8 N_j,\;&& \mbox{in}\quad (0,T)\times {\mathbb T}
nodes.statement_short: Linearized operator about $(h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp)$ with nonlinear forcing $N_1,\dots,N_8$.

nodes.name: Nonlinear terms $N_1,\dots,N_8$
nodes.statement: The nonlinear terms $N_i$, $i=1,\dots,8,$ on the right hand side of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} are defined as \begin{align*} N_1&=\partial_x\left[\left(\frac{f^2}{2}+fh_\sharp\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\ N_2&=\partial_x \left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\left(3h_\sharp^2 f+3f^2h_\sharp+f^3\right)\partial_x f\right],\\ N_3&=-\partial_x \left[\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}\left(3h_\sharp^2 f+3f^2h_\sharp+f^3\right)\partial_x^3 f\right],\\ N_4&=\partial_x \left[\mathcal{A}\frac{f}{h_\sharp^2(1+\frac{f}{h_\sharp})}\partial_x f \right],\\ N_5&=\partial_x\left[\left(\Gamma_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp+\Theta f\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\ N_6&=\partial_x\left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\left(\Gamma_\sharp f^2+2\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp^2+\Theta f^2+2\Theta h_\sharp f\right)\partial_x f\right],\\ N_7&=-\partial_x\left[\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left(\Gamma_\sharp f^2+2\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp^2+\Theta f^2+2\Theta h_\sharp f\right)\partial_x^3 f\right],\\ N_8&=\partial_x \left[\Theta \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^2} \frac{(f^2+2h_\sharp f)\partial_x f }{(h_\sharp+f)^{2}}+\Gamma_\sharp\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^2} \frac{(f^2+2h_\sharp f)\partial_x f }{(h_\sharp+f)^{2}}-\Theta \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^2} \partial_x f \right]\\ &= \partial_x \left[ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2}\frac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{h_\sharp^2(f+h_\sharp)^2}\partial_x f\right]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit formulas for the eight nonlinear terms in the perturbation system.

nodes.name: Smallness restriction on $f$
nodes.statement: \|f\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0}< h_\sharp,
nodes.label: restriction1

nodes.name: Series expansion of $N_4$
nodes.statement: N_4&=\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp^2}\partial_x^2 f +\left(\frac{\partial_x f}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^\infty (-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}-\frac{f}{h_\sharp^3}(\partial_x f)^2\sum_{j=1}^\infty j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]}.
nodes.label: NL4

N_8&=\partial_x \left[  rac{3\mathcal{A}}{2} rac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{h_\sharp^2(f+h_\sharp)^2}\partial_x fight]
onumber\ &=  rac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\left[ rac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left( rac{f}{h_\sharp}+1ight)^2}\partial_x^2 f+ rac{2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left( rac{f}{h_\sharp}+1ight)^2}\partial_x fight]
onumber\ &\quad-  rac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^4}\left[ rac{2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2}{\left( rac{f}{h_\sharp}+1ight)^3} rac{(\partial_x f)^2}{h_\sharp}ight]
onumber\ &= rac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2ight)\partial_x^2 f+\left(2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2ight)\partial_x fight]\sum_{j=1}^\infty j(-1)^{j+1}\left( rac{f}{h_\sharp}ight)^{j-1}

nodes.name: Positivity of G, A, D
nodes.statement: In what follows the constants $\mathcal G,\mathcal A,$ representing the gravitational and van der Waals forces as well as the diffusion coefficient $\mathcal D$ are assumed to be strictly positive.

nodes.name: Weak solution
nodes.statement: Set $\zeta=3$ for the capillary driven flow ($\mathcal{S}>0$) and $\zeta=1$ for the gravity driven flow ($\mathcal{S}=0$).We say that $(f,\Theta)\in \left(L^1(0,T;W^{\zeta,1}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$ is a weak solution of (\ref{eq:systemlinearized}) on $[0,T)$ corresponding to initial data $(f_0,\Theta_0)$ if and only if \begin{align*} -\int_{\mathbb T} f_0\phi(0)dx&-\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T} f\partial_t\phi dxdt+\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T} \partial_x^2\phi\left(-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\Theta +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)f\right) dxdt\\ &+\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T}\partial_x^4\phi \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3f dxdt+\sum_{j=1}^4\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T} \partial_x^{-1}N_j\partial_x \phi dxdt =0 \end{align*} and \begin{align*} -\int_{\mathbb T} \Theta_0\psi(0)dx&-\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T} \Theta\partial_t\psi dxdt+\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T} \partial_x^2\psi\left(-\left(h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\Theta+\left(\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\right)f\right) dxdt\\ &+\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T}\partial_x^4\psi\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2} \Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2f dxdt+\sum_{j=5}^8\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T} \partial_x^{-1}N_j\partial_x \psi dxdt =0 \end{align*} for all $(\phi,\psi)\in C^{\infty}_c([0,T)\times {\mathbb T})$, where $\partial_x^{-1}$ denotes the operator given by $\widehat{\partial_x^{-1}u}(n)=-\frac{i}{n}\hat{u}(n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Weak formulation of the perturbation system tested against $C_c^\infty$ functions, with $\zeta=3$ ($\mathcal S>0$) or $\zeta=1$ ($\mathcal S=0$).
nodes.label: defi1

nodes.name: Energy functional $\mathscr{E}^r_s$
nodes.statement: Let $r,s\geq 0$. For $(f,\Theta):[0,T) \to \dot A^r({\mathbb T})\times \dot A^s({\mathbb T})$, we define the following functional: \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}^r_{s}(f,\Theta):[0,T) \to [0,\infty),\qquad \mathscr{E}^r_{s}(f,\Theta)(t):=\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^r}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^s}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Energy functional (17)
nodes.statement: \mathscr{E}^r_{s}(f,\Theta):[0,T) \to [0,\infty),\qquad \mathscr{E}^r_{s}(f,\Theta)(t):=\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^r}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^s}.
nodes.label: energy

nodes.name: Functions $\Lambda_1$, $\Lambda_2$
nodes.statement: \Lambda_1(t)&:= h_\sharp+\frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3}+ \frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^2}\left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]}+\Gamma_\sharp\nonumber \\ &\quad+\mathcal{G}\left(4\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp +5h_\sharp^2\right)+\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp + \frac{3}{2}h_\sharp + \left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\Big\} ,\\ \Lambda_2(t)&:=\frac{13}{2}h_\sharp+2\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{G}h_\sharp^2+\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\frac{h_\sharp}{2}\,,
nodes.label: eq:Lambda_1

nodes.name: Constants $\mathfrak{C}_1$, $\mathfrak{C}_2$
nodes.statement: \mathfrak{C}_1&:=\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3-\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right|,\\ \mathfrak{C}_2&:=h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}.
nodes.label: constant1

nodes.name: Global existence for S=0
nodes.statement: Let $f_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}), \Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$ be nontrivial initial data for \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} such that $$ \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}. $$ Assume that $\mathfrak{C}_1,\mathfrak{C}_2>0$. If \begin{align*} \gamma_1:=\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(0)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0,\\ \gamma_2:=\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(0)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0, \end{align*} then there exists at least one global solution $(f,\Theta)$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1} with regularity \begin{align*} (f,\Theta)\in &\Big(L^{\frac{2}{r}}\left(0,T;W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^1\left(0,T;C^{1+\alpha}({\mathbb T})\right) \cap L^2(0,T;H^2({\mathbb T}))\Big)^2, \end{align*} for any $r\in[0,2), \alpha\in[0,\frac{1}{2})$ and $T>0$. Moreover, the weak solution satisfies the following exponential decay: $$ \|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}, $$ where \begin{equation} \delta=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2\}>0. \end{equation} Furthermore, if the solution $(f,\Theta)$ satisfies the regularity $$ (f,\Theta)\in \left(L^1\left(0,T;\dot{A}^2({\mathbb T})\right)\right)^2, $$ then the weak solution is unique.
nodes.statement_short: For gravity-driven films ($\mathcal S=0$) with medium-size Wiener-algebra data, global weak solutions exist, decay exponentially, and are unique in $L^1\dot A^2$.

nodes.name: Smallness condition implies positivity
nodes.statement: The condition $ \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\} $ in Theorem \ref{global1} implies in particular that \[ \|f\|_{L^\infty}<\|f_0\|_{\dot A^0}<h_\sharp\quad\mbox{and}\quad \|\Theta\|_{L^\infty}<\|\Theta_0\|_{\dot A^0}<\Gamma_\sharp. \] This corresponds to a positivity condition of $h_0$ and $\Gamma_0$ and ensures that \eqref{restriction1} is initially satisfied.

nodes.name: Explicit example: highly oscillating initial data
nodes.statement: Note that the size restriction is explicitly computable and that the initial data do not need to be small in Sobolev spaces (one should compare the results in this paper with the global result in \cite{bruellwell}). In particular, we prove the existence global weak solutions and their decay towards the flat state for highly oscillating initial data. Let us further explain this with an explicit example. Consider the case where van der Waals forces are neglected, that is $\mathcal A=0$ and set $\mathcal G=\mathcal D=1$. We choose the initial data $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$ to be $$ h_0(x)=1+\mu\sin(1000x)\quad \mbox{and}\quad \Gamma_0(x)=\frac{1}{2}+\mu\cos(1000x), $$ for $0<\mu< \frac{1}{4}$. Then, $$ h_\sharp=1,\quad\Gamma_\sharp=\frac{1}{2},\quad\mathscr{E}^0_0(h_0-h_\sharp,\Gamma_0-\Gamma_\sharp)=2\mu, $$ and the constants $\mathfrak{C}_1,\mathfrak{C}_2,\Lambda_1(0),$ and $\Lambda_2(0)$ are given by $$ \mathfrak{C}_1=\frac{1}{12},\quad\mathfrak{C}_2=1,\quad \Lambda_1(0)= \frac{89}{6},\quad \Lambda_2(0)=\frac{17}{2}. $$ Then, for $\mu<\frac{1}{356}\sim 0.003$, this family of initial data satisfies the hypotheses and Theorem~\ref{global1} guarantees the existence of a global weak solution $(h,\Gamma)$ corresponding to the initial data $(h_0,\Gamma_0)$. Moreover the solution decays exponentially towards the flat equilibrium and \[ \|h(t)-h_\sharp\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Gamma-\Gamma_\sharp\|_{L^\infty}\leq 2\mu e^{-\delta t}, \] where $\delta =\frac{1}{12}-\frac{89}{3}\mu$. Furthermore, observe that $$ \|h_0\|_{\dot{C}^1}=\|\Gamma_0\|_{\dot{C}^1}=O(1) \quad \mbox{while}\quad \|h_0\|_{H^2}=\|\Gamma_0\|_{H^2}=O(10^3). $$
nodes.statement_short: For $h_0=1+\mu\sin(1000x)$, $\Gamma_0=1/2+\mu\cos(1000x)$ with $\mu<1/356$, Theorem 1 applies although the $H^2$ norms are $O(10^3)$.

If \begin{align*} \gamma_1:=\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(0)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0,\\ \gamma_2:=\mathfrak{C}_2-\left(\Lambda_2(0)+\frac{\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2}{2}\right)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0,\\ \gamma_3:=\mathfrak{C}_3-\Lambda_3\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)&>0, \end{align*} then there exists at least one global solution $(f,\Theta)$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1} with regularity \begin{align*} f\in & L^\frac{4}{s}\left(0,T; W^{s,\infty}({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^{1}\left(0,T;C^{3+\alpha}({\mathbb T})\right) \cap L^2\left(0,T;H^2({\mathbb T})\right),\quad s\in[0,4),\\ \Theta\in & L^\frac{4}{r}\left(0,T; W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^{1}\left(0,T;C^{1+\alpha}({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^2\left(0,T;H^1({\mathbb T})\right),\quad r\in[0,2) \end{align*} for any $T$ and $0\leq\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$. Moreover, the weak solutions satisfies the following exponential decay: $$ \|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}, $$ where \begin{equation} \delta=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3\}>0. \end{equation} Furthermore, if the solution $(f,\Theta)$ satisfies the regularity $$ (f,\Theta)\in L^1\left(0,T;\dot{A}^4({\mathbb T})\right)\times L^1\left(0,T;\dot{A}^2({\mathbb T})\right), $$ then the weak solution is unique.

nodes.name: Proof outline of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Let us start by outlining the steps of the proof. First, we provide in Subsection \ref{ss:e} some \emph{a priori} estimates of a solution $(f,\Theta)\in \left(C^1(0,T;\dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}. Under the assumptions on the initial data in Theorem \ref{global1}, which in particular require that \[ \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}, \] we will show that the solution $(f,\Theta)$ preserves this estimate, that is $$ \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T. $$ Notice that the above inequality implies that $$ \|f(t)\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}<h_\sharp \quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T, $$ $$ \|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}<\Gamma_\sharp \quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T. $$ Hence, the positivity conditions for $h$ and $\Gamma$, $$ \|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|f(t)\|_{\dot A^0} < h_\sharp,\quad \|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot A^0}<\Gamma_\sharp $$ are preserved for all $t\in [0,T)$. Then we obtain that, for small enough initial energy $\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)$, the following inequality holds: $$ \frac{d}{dt} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+\delta \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\leq 0 $$ for some $\delta>0$ dependent on the initial data. This inequality implies that a local solution $(f,\Theta)$ can not leave a ball in $(L^\infty((0,T); \dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\cap L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T})))^2$; thus, there is no finite time singularity in these functional spaces. In Subsection \ref{ss:gl} we implement a standard Galerkin approximation argument to prove the existence of global weak solutions. The existence of a classical local solution of the Galerkin approximated sytem is guaranteed by the Picard--Lindel\"of Theorem. These approximated solutions $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in {\mathbb N}}$ are analytic. In particular, they satisfy $$ (f_M,\Theta_M)\in \left(C^1([0,T_M); \dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2, $$ where $T_M>0$ denotes the maximal time of existence of $(f_M,\Theta_M)$. The \emph{a priori} estimates from before ensure the \emph{global} existence of the approximated solutions and provide the necessary \emph{a priori} bounds in order to use compactness arguments and pass to the limit $M\to \infty$, which yields a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}. Now, let $(f_M,\Theta_M)$ be such approximate solution corresponding to the initial data $(f_0,\Theta_0)$, which satisfy the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{global1}, then, in view of the Poincar\'e-like inequality in \eqref{lem:P}, we see that $\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)$ is a Lyapunov functional, \emph{i.e.}, that $$ \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)+\delta \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(0)\leq 0 \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<\infty. $$ The latter implies the exponential decay towards the equilibrium $(f^*,\Theta^*)=(0,0)$ for the global weak solution (see Subsection \ref{ss:decay}). Eventually, in Subsection \ref{ss:unique} it is shown that a global weak solution in $$ \left(L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2 $$ is unique.
nodes.section: 4 Proof of Theorem 1: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}=0$
nodes.statement_short: A priori Wiener-algebra energy estimates, Galerkin approximation with compactness, Lyapunov decay, Gronwall uniqueness. Key: smallness of $\mathscr E^0_0$ is propagated, giving $\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr E^0_0+\delta\mathscr E^2_2\le0$.

nodes.name: A priori estimates in the Wiener algebra (S=0)
nodes.statement: Let $T\in (0,\infty]$ and $$ (f,\Theta)\in \left( C^1([0,T), \dot A({\mathbb T}))\right)^2 $$ be a local solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} with initial data $$ (f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A({\mathbb T})\right)^2 $$ satisfying the condition \[ \mathcal{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}. \] By continuity there exists $0<t_*\leq T$ such that the above estimate is satisfied on $[0,t_*)$, that is \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_*). \end{equation} Let us moreover assume that $t_*$ is the maximal time such that \eqref{eq:t} holds true on $[0,t_*)$. Hence, either \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_*)=\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\} \end{equation} or $t_*=T$. Notice that the restriction \eqref{restriction1} holds true on the time interval $[0,t_*)$. In the following let $t\in [0,t_*)$. We compute \begin{align*} \partial_t|\hat{f}(k)| &=\frac{\text{Re}\left(\bar{\hat{f}}(k)\partial_t\hat{f}(k)\right)}{|\hat{f}(k)|}, \end{align*} so, using that $\mathcal{S}=0$, \begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_4\|_{\dot A^0} ,\\ \frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right| \|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_5\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_6\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0} \end{align} We recall that \begin{align*} \widehat{uv}(k)=\sum_{j\in{\mathbb Z}}\hat{u}(j)\hat{v}(k-j) \end{align*} and by the hypothesis of the theorem \[ \|f\|_{\dot A^0}\leq h_\sharp,\qquad \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \Gamma_\sharp. \] Using the algebra property of the Wiener space $A^s({\mathbb T})$, \emph{i.e.} $$ \|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2^{s}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}\|g\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})},\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad \, f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T}),\quad s\in{\mathbb N}, $$ together with the interpolation inequality $$ \|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}({\mathbb T})}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0({\mathbb T})}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}^{\theta},\quad \mbox{for all} \quad 0<\theta<1,\quad s\geq0, $$ the contribution of the nonlinear terms $N_k$, $k=1,2,$ and $4$, can be estimated as \begin{align*} \|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2}{2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left(\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\\ &\leq \left(\frac{3}{2}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \frac{5}{2}h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,, \end{align*} \begin{align*} \|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\bigg[\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2h_\sharp+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^3\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\quad+\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{A^1}+6\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\bigg]\\ &\leq\frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\leq \frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,, \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \|N_4\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^\infty\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\\ &\quad +\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\\ &\quad+\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]}\\ &\leq \mathcal{A} \bigg{]} , \end{align*} where we used the convergence of the geometric series $\sum_{j=1}^\infty r^{j-1}$ for $|r|<1$, and \[ \sum_{j=1}^\infty jr^{j-1}=\partial_r \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}r^j = A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}\\ &\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\bigg{[}\left(3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp+\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} h_\sharp\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\quad+\left(4\|f\|_{\dot
