\end{align*} Grouping terms, we find that \begin{align*} \|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\ &\qquad + h_\sharp \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}\\ &\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\ &\qquad + h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}. \end{align*} We recall the definition \eqref{constant1} and \eqref{constant2}, then we add equations \eqref{eq:1} and \eqref{eq:2}, use the previous estimates for $N_j$, $j=1,2,4,5,6,$ and 8 and obtain that \begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&\leq -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2} \end{align} for $t\in[0,t_*)$, with $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ defined in \eqref{eq:Lambda_1} and \eqref{eq:Lambda_2}, respectively. Using the hypothesis of the Theorem \ref{global1}, we have that \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\bigg{|}_{t=0}&<0, \end{align*} so, there exists a time $0<t_0\leq t_*$ such that \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0]. \end{equation} Let us assume that $t_0$ is the maximal times such that \eqref{eq:estimate} holds true on $[0,t_0]$ We want to propagate this decay for all times, that is, we aim to show that $t_0=t_*$, which in turn implies that $t_0=t_*=T$, by \eqref{eq:O1}. Let us emphasize that $\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)$ for $t\in [0,t_0]$ guarantees that \begin{equation} \Lambda_j(t)\leq \Lambda_j(0),\qquad j=1,2 \qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0]. \end{equation} Thereby, for any $t\in [0,t_0]$ we have that $$ \mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\geq \mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(0)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)=\gamma_1>0, $$ $$ \mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\geq \mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(0)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)=\gamma_2>0. $$ In particular, we obtain that \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&< 0\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0). \end{align*} Assume that $t_0<t_*$. By continuity, we deduce that $\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_0)=\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(0)$, but this implies that, again, \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\bigg{|}_{t=t_0}&\leq 0, \end{align*} and that contradicts the assumption $t_0<t_*$. Thus, we have shown that in fact \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,t_*) \end{equation} and thereby $t_*=T$, in view of \eqref{eq:O1}. Then, \begin{equation} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq -\gamma \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T), \end{equation} where $\delta:=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2\}$. Eventually, the energy estimate for the gravity driven equation ($\mathcal S =0$) reads \[ \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+\delta\int_0^t \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(\tau)\, d\tau \leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0) \] and \[ \int_0^t \|\partial_t f(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\partial_t \Theta(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}\, d\tau\leq c, \] for all $t\in[0,T)$, where $c>0$ is a constant depending on the initial data.
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $\frac{d}{dt}\|\cdot\|_{\dot A^0}$ using the algebra and interpolation inequalities, then a continuity/contradiction argument propagates smallness. Key: $\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr E^0_0\le-(\mathfrak C_1-\Lambda_1\mathscr E^0_0)\|f\|_{\dot A^2}-(\mathfrak C_2-\Lambda_2\mathscr E^0_0)\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}$.

nodes.name: Existence of global weak solutions (S=0)
nodes.statement: We use a standard Galerkin approximation to obtain in the limit a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} where surface tension effects are neglected, \emph{i.~e.} $\mathcal{S}=0$. Let us fix $M\in {\mathbb Z}^+$. Set \[ f_M(t,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat f(t,k)e^{ikx}\qquad \mbox{and}\qquad \Theta_M(t,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat \theta(t,k)e^{ikx} \] and the initial data \[ f_M(0,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat f_0(k)e^{ikx}\qquad \mbox{and}\qquad \Theta_M(0,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat \theta_0(k)e^{ikx} \] to coincide with the Fourier truncation of the $f_0$ and $\Theta_0$, respectively. Recall that the convergence of the Fourier series of the initial data is guaranteed by the assumption that $f_0,\Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$. We consider the Galerkin approximated problems: \begin{alignat*}{2} \partial_t f_M-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\partial_x^2 \Theta_M +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\partial_x^2 f_M+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\partial_x^4 f_M&=\sum_{j=1,2,4} N_j^M,\; && \text{ in }(0,T)\times{\mathbb T}\\ \partial_t \Theta_M -\left(h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\partial_x^2\Theta_M+\left(\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\right) \partial_x^2f_M+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2 \partial_x^4f_M &= \sum_{j=5,6,8} N_j^M,\;&& \text{ in }(0,T)\times{\mathbb T} \end{alignat*} where the nonlinearities $N_j^M$ are given by \begin{align*} N_1^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\left(\frac{f^2}{2}+fh_\sharp\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\ N_2^M&=\partial_x P_M \left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\left(3h_\sharp^2 f+3f^2h_\sharp+f^3\right)\partial_x f\right],\\ N_4^M&=\mathcal{A} P_M \bigg{[}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp^2}\partial_x^2 f +\left(\frac{\partial_x f}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^M (-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}-\frac{f}{h_\sharp^3}(\partial_x f)^2\sum_{j=1}^M j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]},\\ N_5^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\left(\Gamma_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp+\Theta f\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\ N_6^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\left(\Gamma_\sharp f^2+2\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp^2+\Theta f^2+2\Theta h_\sharp f\right)\partial_x f\right],\\ N_8^M&=\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4} P_M\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x^2 f+\left(2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x f\right]\sum_{j=1}^M j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\nonumber\\ &\quad- \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^4} P_M\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\frac{(\partial_x f)^2}{h_\sharp}\right]\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=2}^M j(j-1)(-1)^{j}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}. \end{align*} Here, the operator $P_M$ denotes the Fourier truncation operator \[ P_M g(x)=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat g(k)e^{ikx}\qquad\mbox{for any}\quad g\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}). \] The Picard--Lindel\"of Theorem ensures the existence of classical solutions \[ f_M,\Theta_M\in C^1([0,T_M);C^\infty({\mathbb T})), \] where $T_M>0$ is the maximal existence time. Furthermore, the approximated problems provide the same \emph{a priori} bounds as in the previous sections. Consequently the Galerkin solutions $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in {\mathbb N}}$ exist globally and for any $T>0$ we have the bounds: \begin{equation} (f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \quad \mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left( L^\infty\left(0,T;\dot A^0({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^1\left(0,T; \dot A^2({\mathbb T}) \right)\right)^2 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} (\partial_t f_M,\partial_t\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \quad \mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left( L^1\left(0,T; \dot A^0({\mathbb T}) \right)\right)^2. \end{equation} Following the lines in \cite{BG18}, the above uniform regularities of the Galerkin approximations $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} $ guarantee the existence of a weakly convergent subsequences (not relabeled) such that \begin{align*} (f_M,\Theta_M)\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup} (f,\Theta)\text { in $\left(L^{\infty}(0,T;L^\infty({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$}. \end{align*} Similarly, using interpolation in Wiener spaces, the finite measure of the spatial domain and the fact that $\dot A^r({\mathbb T})\subset \dot W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T})$ for any $r\geq 0$, we obtain the existence of a subsequence (not relabeled), such that \begin{align} (f_M,\Theta_M)\rightharpoonup (f,\Theta)\text { in $\left(L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T;\dot W^{r,p}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$},\qquad 0\leq r<2,\;\;1\leq p<\infty. \end{align} From the previous fact we can infer that actually $$ (f,\Theta) \in \left(L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T;\dot W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2,\qquad 0\leq r<2. $$ Furthermore \eqref{boundedness}, \eqref{boundednesst} imply that $$ (f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \text{ is uniformly bounded in } \left(L^2(0,T;H^{1}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2, $$ which is due to $\dot A^s({\mathbb T})\subset \dot H^s({\mathbb T})$ for any $s \geq 0$ and an interpolation inequality for fractional Sobolev spaces. Eventually, as a consequence of \eqref{boundedness},\eqref{boundednesst} and a compactness argument as in \cite[Corollary 4]{simon1986compact}, we obtain (up to a subsequence) that $$ (f_M,\Theta_M)\rightarrow (f,\Theta)\qquad \text{ in $\left(L^1(0,T;{C}^{1+s}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$}, \quad \,0\leq s<\frac{1}{2}. $$ Passing to the limit in the weak formulation of the Galerkin approximation yields the existence of a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}.
nodes.statement_short: Galerkin approximation: Picard-Lindelof local solutions, global by a priori bounds, then compactness (Aubin-Lions type) and passage to the limit.

nodes.name: Exponential trend to equilibrium (S=0)
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{eq:energyE} and the definition of $\delta>0$ in \eqref{delta}, we have that \begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq -\delta\mathscr{E}^2_2(f_M,\Theta_M)(t) \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0. \end{align} Using the Poincar\'e-like inequality \eqref{lem:P}, we also conclude that $$ \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq -\delta\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t) \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0, $$ which in turn implies the exponential decay towards the equilibrium: \[ \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0. \] Using \eqref{eq:Linf1} and the lower semi-continuity of the weak$-*$ convergence, we have that \begin{equation*} \|f(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}\leq \liminf_{k\to \infty}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Energy inequality plus Poincare-like inequality gives $\frac{d}{dt}\mathscr E\le-\delta\mathscr E$; Gronwall and weak-* lower semicontinuity pass decay to the limit.

nodes.name: Uniqueness (S=0)
nodes.statement: The proof follows a standard contradiction argument. For the sake of brevity, we only sketch the idea. Assume that there exist two different solutions $(f_1,\Theta_1)$ and $(f_2,\Theta_2)$ starting from the same initial data $$ (f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A^0({\mathbb T})\right)^2. $$ Assume also that these solutions satisfy $$ (f_i,\Theta_i)\in \left( L^{1}(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2. $$ Using the smallness of the initial data, the same estimates as in Subsection \ref{ss:e} yield that \begin{multline*} \frac{d}{dt}\left(\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\\ \leq C\left[\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right]\left(\|f_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|f_2\|_{\dot A^2}+\|\Theta_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^2}+1\right). \end{multline*} Now the statement is a consequence of Gronwall's inequality and the fact that $(f_1,\Theta_1)(0)=(f_2,\Theta_2)(0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: estimate the $\dot A^0$ difference of two solutions and apply Gronwall's inequality.

nodes.name: Proof outline of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: The proof essentially follows the arguments in the previous section, the main difference relying in the fact that for $\mathcal S>0$ we have that \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} is a system of mixed orders. Thereby the energy estimates require some additional investigation. The existence of local solutions of the approximated Galerkin systems are straightforward due to Picard--Lindel\"of's theorem (see Subsection \ref{ss:gl}). The energy estimates then ensure that the approximated solutions exist globally. Furthermore, the energy estimates provide the necessary a priori bounds to pass to the limit in the Galerkin approximation; thereby guaranteeing the existence of a global weak solution in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}. In view of the weak lower semicontinuity of the norm, the global weak solution inherits the energy estimates for the approximated solutions and we can conclude the regularity and exponential decay of the solution.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of Theorem 2: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}>0$
nodes.statement_short: Same scheme as for $\mathcal S=0$ (Galerkin, energy estimates, limit), with extra estimates for the fourth-order terms.

nodes.name: A priori estimates in the Wiener algebra (S>0)
nodes.statement: To perform our energy estimates let us assume that there exists a local solution $$ (f,\Theta)\in \left(C^1([0,T), \dot A^0({\mathbb T})) \right)^2 $$ of the fourth-order system \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} where $\mathcal{S}>0$, corresponding to initial data $(f_0,\Theta_0)$, satisfying \[ \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}. \] Similar as before, we have that \begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2} - \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\|f\|_{\dot A^4}+\sum_{j=1}^4\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0} ,\\ \frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right|\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}h_\sharp^2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^4} +\sum_{j=5}^8\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0}. \end{align} Keeping in mind the definitions of $\mathfrak{C_i}$, $i=1,2,3,$ in \eqref{constant1}, \eqref{constant2}, and \eqref{constant3}, we take the sum of the two inequalities above and obtain that $$ \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)+\mathfrak{C}_1\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\mathfrak{C}_2\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\mathfrak{C}_3\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\leq \sum_{j=1}^8\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0}. $$ Recalling \eqref{eq:energyE}, we have that \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}&\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)+\mathfrak{C}_3\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\\ &\leq \|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_7\|_{\dot A^0} -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}, \end{align*} where $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are defined in \eqref{eq:Lambda_1} and \eqref{eq:Lambda_2}, respectively. Thus we are left to estimate the remaining terms $\|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}$ and $\|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}$. Similarly as before, using the interpolation inequality in Wiener spaces, we estimate \begin{align*} \|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{19}{3}\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}, \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left(6\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+h_\sharp^2\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\\ &\quad +\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left(8\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{A^1}+4\|\Theta\|_{A^1}h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}. \end{align*} Note that by Young's inequality, we have that $$ \|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}\leq \|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^{\frac{1}{4}}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}^{\frac{3}{4}}\leq\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\left(\frac{1}{4\varepsilon}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\frac{3\varepsilon}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\right), $$ for any $\varepsilon>0$. In particular, as $\Theta$ and $f$ are nonzero (provided the initial data are nontrivial), we can take $$ \varepsilon=\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}}. $$ Thus, $$ \|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}\leq\frac{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}^2}{4\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\frac{3\mathscr{E}_0^0}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\leq \frac{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{4}+\frac{3\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}. $$ Then, we conclude that \[ \|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left( (14h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp +4h_\sharp^2)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \|f\|_{\dot A^4}+h_\sharp^2\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}\right). \] Using \eqref{eq:Lambda_3}, we can group terms as follows: \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)&\leq -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\left(\Lambda_2(t)+\frac{\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2}{2}\right)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\quad-\left(\mathfrak{C}_3-\Lambda_3\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^4}. \end{align*} Repeating the argument from Section \ref{S:T1}, we conclude that \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t} \end{equation} where $\delta$ is defined in \eqref{delta}. The energy estimate for the capillary driven thin film ($\mathcal S >0$) reads \begin{equation*} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+ \int_0^t\delta \mathscr{E}^4_2(f,\Theta)(\tau)\, d\tau \leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0) \end{equation*} and \[ \int_0^t \|\partial_t f(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\partial_t \Theta(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}\,d\tau \leq c, \] for all $t\in[0,T)$, where $c>0$ is a constant depending on the initial data.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the $\mathcal S=0$ estimates and additionally bound $N_3,N_7$ using interpolation and Young's inequality with a solution-dependent $\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Existence of global weak solutions (S>0)
nodes.statement: In a similar way as in Subsection \ref{ss:gl}, we obtain the existence of a sequence of global Galerkin approximations $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}$. Then, the energy estimates from above guarantee that for any $T>0$: $$ (f_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}\quad\mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad L^\infty(0,T; A^0({\mathbb T}))\cap L^1(0,T;A^4({\mathbb T}))\subset L^2(0,T;H^2({\mathbb T})) $$ and $$ (\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}\quad\mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad L^\infty(0,T; A^0({\mathbb T}))\cap L^1(0,T;A^2({\mathbb T}))\subset L^2(0,T;H^1({\mathbb T})). $$ Moreover, the time derivatives satisfy $$ (\partial_t f_M,\partial_t \Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}\quad\mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left(L^1(0,T;A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2 $$ for any $T>0$. Consequently, we obtain the existence of a subsequence (not relabeled) such that \begin{align} \begin{split} &f_M\rightharpoonup f\text { in $L^{\frac{4}{s}}(0,T; W^{s,p}({\mathbb T}))$},\quad 0\leq s<4,\;\;1\leq p<\infty\\ &\Theta_M\rightharpoonup \Theta\text { in $L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T; W^{r,p}({\mathbb T}))$} ,\quad 0\leq r<2,\;\;1\leq p<\infty. \end{split} \end{align} Moreover, \begin{align*} f_M&\rightarrow f\qquad \text{ in $L^1(0,T;C^{3+\alpha}({\mathbb T}))$}, \quad \,0\leq \alpha<\frac{1}{2},\\ f_M&\rightharpoonup f\qquad \text{ in $L^2(0,T, H^2({\mathbb T}))$} \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \Theta_M&\rightarrow \Theta\qquad \text{ in $L^1(0,T;C^{1+\alpha}({\mathbb T}))$},\quad \,0\leq \alpha<\frac{1}{2},\\ \Theta_M&\rightharpoonup \Theta\qquad \text{ in $L^2(0,T, H^1({\mathbb T}))$}. \end{align*} Equipped with these convergences we can pass to the limit in the weak formulation and conclude the global existence of a weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} for $\mathcal S>0$ in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}.
nodes.statement_short: Galerkin approximations with uniform bounds from the energy estimates; compactness and passage to the limit.

nodes.name: Exponential trend to equilibrium (S>0)
nodes.statement: The proof follows the same ideas as in Subsection~\ref{ss:decay}. The sequence of Galerkin approximation $(f_M, \Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}$ satisfies the energy estimates. In particular, we have the exponential decay towards the equilibrum in \eqref{eq:Es}: \[ \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0, \] where $\delta>0$ is defined in \eqref{delta}. Using \eqref{eq:Linf} and the lower semi-continuity of the weak$-*$ convergence, we have that \begin{equation*} \|f(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}\leq \liminf_{k\to \infty}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t} \end{equation*} for all $t\geq 0$, which proves the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Galerkin approximations decay exponentially; lower semicontinuity transfers the decay to the weak solution.

nodes.name: Uniqueness (S>0)
nodes.statement: Also the proof for the conditional uniqueness is similar to the one in Subsection \ref{ss:unique}. Assume that there exist two different solutions $(f_1,\Theta_1)$ and $(f_2,\Theta_2)$ starting from the same initial data $$ (f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A({\mathbb T})\right)^2. $$ Moreover, we suppose that the solutions satisfy the additional regularity $$ (f_i,\Theta_i)\in \left( L^{1}(0,T;\dot A^4({\mathbb T}))\times L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2 $$ for $i=1,2$. Similar as for the energy estimate we compute that \begin{multline*} \frac{d}{dt}\left(\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\\ \leq C \left[\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right]\\ \times\left(\|f_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|f_2\|_{\dot A^2}+\|f_1\|_{\dot A^4}+\|f_2\|_{\dot A^4}+\|\Theta_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^2}\right). \end{multline*} Now the assertion follows by applying Gronwall's inequality and recalling that the solutions $(f_i,\Theta_i), i=1,2$ share the same initial data.
nodes.statement_short: Estimate the $\dot A^0$ difference of two solutions and apply Gronwall's inequality.

nodes.name: Smallness on $[0,t_*)$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_*).
nodes.label: eq:t

nodes.name: Alternative at maximal time $t_*$
nodes.statement: \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_*)=\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}
nodes.label: eq:O1

nodes.name: Wiener-norm derivative bounds (S=0)
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_4\|_{\dot A^0},\\ \frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right| \|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_5\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_6\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}
nodes.label: eq:1

nodes.name: Differential energy inequality (S=0)
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&\leq -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}
nodes.label: eq:energyE

nodes.name: Energy bounded by initial energy on $[0,t_0]$
nodes.statement: \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0].
nodes.label: eq:estimate

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\Lambda_j$
nodes.statement: \Lambda_j(t)\leq \Lambda_j(0),\qquad j=1,2 \qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0].
nodes.label: eq:Ldecay

nodes.name: Energy bounded by initial energy on $[0,t_*)$
nodes.statement: \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,t_*)
nodes.label: eq:Edecay

nodes.name: Dissipative energy inequality
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq -\gamma \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T),
nodes.label: eq:E

nodes.name: Uniform bounds on Galerkin approximations
nodes.statement: (f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \quad \mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left( L^\infty\left(0,T;\dot A^0({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^1\left(0,T; \dot A^2({\mathbb T}) \right)\right)^2
nodes.label: boundedness

nodes.name: Uniform bounds on time derivatives
nodes.statement: (\partial_t f_M,\partial_t\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \quad \mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left( L^1\left(0,T; \dot A^0({\mathbb T}) \right)\right)^2.
nodes.label: boundednesst

nodes.name: Weak convergence of Galerkin approximations (S=0)
nodes.statement: (f_M,\Theta_M)\rightharpoonup (f,\Theta)\text { in $\left(L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T;\dot W^{r,p}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$},\qquad 0\leq r<2,\;\;1\leq p<\infty.
nodes.label: eq:Linf1

nodes.name: Energy dissipation for Galerkin approximations
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq -\delta\mathscr{E}^2_2(f_M,\Theta_M)(t) \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0.
nodes.label: eq:expdecay

nodes.name: Wiener-norm derivative bounds (S>0)
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2} - \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\|f\|_{\dot A^4}+\sum_{j=1}^4\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0},\\ \frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right|\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}h_\sharp^2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^4} +\sum_{j=5}^8\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0}.
nodes.label: eq:1b

nodes.name: Exponential decay of the energy (S>0)
nodes.statement: \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}
nodes.label: eq:Es

nodes.name: Weak convergence of Galerkin approximations (S>0)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} &f_M\rightharpoonup f\text { in $L^{\frac{4}{s}}(0,T; W^{s,p}({\mathbb T}))$},\quad 0\leq s<4,\;\;1\leq p<\infty\\ &\Theta_M\rightharpoonup \Theta\text { in $L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T; W^{r,p}({\mathbb T}))$} ,\quad 0\leq r<2,\;\;1\leq p<\infty. \end{split}
nodes.label: eq:Linf

nodes.name: Outline
nodes.statement: Let us start by outlining the steps of the proof. First, we provide in Subsection \ref{ss:e} some \emph{a priori} estimates of a solution $(f,\Theta)\in \left(C^1(0,T;\dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$ of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized}.
nodes.section: 4 Proof of Theorem 1: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}=0$
nodes.statement_short: Plan: start from a priori estimates in $\dot A^0$.

nodes.name: Smallness propagated
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions on the initial data in Theorem \ref{global1}, which in particular require that \[ \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}, \] we will show that the solution $(f,\Theta)$ preserves this estimate, that is $$ \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T. $$ Notice that the above inequality implies that $$ \|f(t)\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}<h_\sharp \quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T, $$ $$ \|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}<\Gamma_\sharp \quad\mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<T. $$ Hence, the positivity conditions for $h$ and $\Gamma$, $$ \|f(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|f(t)\|_{\dot A^0} < h_\sharp,\quad \|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty}\leq \|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot A^0}<\Gamma_\sharp $$ are preserved for all $t\in [0,T)$.
nodes.section: 4 Proof of Theorem 1: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}=0$
nodes.statement_short: The smallness of the energy is preserved, hence positivity of $h$ and $\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Energy inequality
nodes.statement: Then we obtain that, for small enough initial energy $\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)$, the following inequality holds: $$ \frac{d}{dt} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+\delta \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\leq 0 $$ for some $\delta>0$ dependent on the initial data. This inequality implies that a local solution $(f,\Theta)$ can not leave a ball in $(L^\infty((0,T); \dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\cap L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T})))^2$; thus, there is no finite time singularity in these functional spaces.
nodes.section: 4 Proof of Theorem 1: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}=0$
nodes.statement_short: Differential energy inequality rules out finite-time singularities.

nodes.name: Galerkin scheme
nodes.statement: In Subsection \ref{ss:gl} we implement a standard Galerkin approximation argument to prove the existence of global weak solutions. The existence of a classical local solution of the Galerkin approximated sytem is guaranteed by the Picard--Lindel\"of Theorem. These approximated solutions $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in {\mathbb N}}$ are analytic. In particular, they satisfy $$ (f_M,\Theta_M)\in \left(C^1([0,T_M); \dot A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2, $$ where $T_M>0$ denotes the maximal time of existence of $(f_M,\Theta_M)$. The \emph{a priori} estimates from before ensure the \emph{global} existence of the approximated solutions and provide the necessary \emph{a priori} bounds in order to use compactness arguments and pass to the limit $M\to \infty$, which yields a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}.
nodes.section: 4 Proof of Theorem 1: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}=0$
nodes.statement_short: Galerkin approximations via Picard-Lindelof, global by a priori bounds, limit by compactness.

nodes.name: Lyapunov decay
nodes.statement: Now, let $(f_M,\Theta_M)$ be such approximate solution corresponding to the initial data $(f_0,\Theta_0)$, which satisfy the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{global1}, then, in view of the Poincar\'e-like inequality in \eqref{lem:P}, we see that $\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)$ is a Lyapunov functional, \emph{i.e.}, that $$ \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)+\delta \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(0)\leq 0 \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad 0<t<\infty. $$ The latter implies the exponential decay towards the equilibrium $(f^*,\Theta^*)=(0,0)$ for the global weak solution (see Subsection \ref{ss:decay}).
nodes.section: 4 Proof of Theorem 1: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}=0$
nodes.statement_short: Poincare-like inequality makes the energy a Lyapunov functional: exponential decay.

nodes.name: Uniqueness
nodes.statement: Eventually, in Subsection \ref{ss:unique} it is shown that a global weak solution in $$ \left(L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2 $$ is unique.
nodes.section: 4 Proof of Theorem 1: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}=0$
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness in $L^1\dot A^2$.

nodes.name: Local solution and maximal time
nodes.statement: Let $T\in (0,\infty]$ and $$ (f,\Theta)\in \left( C^1([0,T), \dot A({\mathbb T}))\right)^2 $$ be a local solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} with initial data $$ (f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A({\mathbb T})\right)^2 $$ satisfying the condition \[ \mathcal{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}. \] By continuity there exists $0<t_*\leq T$ such that the above estimate is satisfied on $[0,t_*)$, that is \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_*). \end{equation} Let us moreover assume that $t_*$ is the maximal time such that \eqref{eq:t} holds true on $[0,t_*)$. Hence, either \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_*)=\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\} \end{equation} or $t_*=T$. Notice that the restriction \eqref{restriction1} holds true on the time interval $[0,t_*)$. In the following let $t\in [0,t_*)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a local solution and the maximal time $t_*$ on which the smallness holds.

nodes.name: Derivative of Wiener norms
nodes.statement: We compute \begin{align*} \partial_t|\hat{f}(k)| &=\frac{\text{Re}\left(\bar{\hat{f}}(k)\partial_t\hat{f}(k)\right)}{|\hat{f}(k)|}, \end{align*} so, using that $\mathcal{S}=0$, \begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_4\|_{\dot A^0} ,\\ \frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right| \|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|N_5\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_6\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_8\|_{\dot A^0} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate $|\hat f(k)|$ to bound $\frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}$ and $\frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}$.

nodes.name: Bounds on N1, N2, N4
nodes.statement: We recall that \begin{align*} \widehat{uv}(k)=\sum_{j\in{\mathbb Z}}\hat{u}(j)\hat{v}(k-j) \end{align*} and by the hypothesis of the theorem \[ \|f\|_{\dot A^0}\leq h_\sharp,\qquad \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \Gamma_\sharp. \] Using the algebra property of the Wiener space $A^s({\mathbb T})$, \emph{i.e.} $$ \|fg\|_{\dot{A}^s}\leq 2^{s}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}\|g\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})},\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad \, f,g\in \dot A^s({\mathbb T}),\quad s\in{\mathbb N}, $$ together with the interpolation inequality $$ \|f\|_{\dot{A}^{s\theta}({\mathbb T})}\leq \|f\|_{\dot A^0({\mathbb T})}^{1-\theta}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^s({\mathbb T})}^{\theta},\quad \mbox{for all} \quad 0<\theta<1,\quad s\geq0, $$ the contribution of the nonlinear terms $N_k$, $k=1,2,$ and $4$, can be estimated as \begin{align*} \|N_1\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2}{2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left(\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}h_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\\ &\leq \left(\frac{3}{2}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \frac{5}{2}h_\sharp\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,, \end{align*} \begin{align*} \|N_2\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\bigg[\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2h_\sharp+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^3\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\quad+\left(3h_\sharp^2 \|f\|_{A^1}+6\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp+3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^2\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}\bigg]\\ &\leq\frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\leq \frac{19h_\sharp^2\mathcal{ G}}{3} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,, \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \|N_4\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^\infty\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\\ &\quad +\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\sum_{j=1}^\infty j\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]}\\ &\leq\mathcal{A} \bigg{[}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp} +\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\\ &\quad+\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^1}}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2} \bigg{]}\\ &\leq\mathcal{A} \frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]}\\ &\leq \mathcal{A} \frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{h_\sharp}\frac{\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}}{h_\sharp}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}\bigg{[}2+\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1} \bigg{]} , \end{align*} where we used the convergence of the geometric series $\sum_{j=1}^\infty r^{j-1}$ for $|r|<1$, and \[ \sum_{j=1}^\infty jr^{j-1}=\partial_r \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}r^j = \frac{1}{(1-r)^2},\qquad |r|<1. \]
nodes.statement_short: Algebra and interpolation inequalities bound $N_1,N_2,N_4$.

nodes.name: Bounds on N5, N6, N8
nodes.statement: Similarly, the nonlinear terms $N_j$, $j=5,6,$ and $8$ are bounded by \begin{align*} \|N_5\|_{\dot A^0} &\leq \left(\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\left(4h_\sharp+\Gamma_\sharp\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} \right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+ \Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left(4h_\sharp+2\Gamma_\sharp \right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+ \Gamma_\sharp\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\,,\end{align*} \begin{align*} \|N_6\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\mathcal{G}\left[\left(4\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+4\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp^2\left(\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right)\right]\\ &\leq \mathcal{G}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left[\left(4\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp +4h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+h_\sharp^2\left(\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right)\right]\,, \end{align*} \begin{align*} \|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4}\bigg{[}\left(3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\quad+\left(4\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\left[\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right] \right)\bigg{]}\sum_{j=1}^\infty j\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\nonumber\\ &\quad+ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^3}\left[2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right]\sum_{j=2}^\infty j(j-1)\left(\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}\\ &\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\bigg{[}\left(3\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp+\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0} h_\sharp\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\quad+\left(4\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\frac{h_\sharp}{2}\left[\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right] \right)\bigg{]}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\nonumber\\ &\quad+ \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^3}\left[2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}\right]\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-3}. \end{align*} Grouping terms, we find that \begin{align*} \|N_8\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\ &\qquad + h_\sharp \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^0}\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}\\ &\leq \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^3}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-2}\Big\{7\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2} + \frac{1}{2}h_\sharp[\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+{\frac{h_\sharp}{2}}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}] \\ &\qquad + h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^2}+ \left(1-\frac{\|f\|_{\dot A^0}}{h_\sharp}\right)^{-1}4\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^2}\Big\}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Same estimates for $N_5,N_6,N_8$.

nodes.name: Energy inequality (30)
nodes.statement: We recall the definition \eqref{constant1} and \eqref{constant2}, then we add equations \eqref{eq:1} and \eqref{eq:2}, use the previous estimates for $N_j$, $j=1,2,4,5,6,$ and 8 and obtain that \begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&\leq -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2} \end{align} for $t\in[0,t_*)$, with $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ defined in \eqref{eq:Lambda_1} and \eqref{eq:Lambda_2}, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the estimates to get the differential energy inequality.

nodes.name: Initial decrease
nodes.statement: Using the hypothesis of the Theorem \ref{global1}, we have that \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\bigg{|}_{t=0}&<0, \end{align*} so, there exists a time $0<t_0\leq t_*$ such that \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0]. \end{equation} Let us assume that $t_0$ is the maximal times such that \eqref{eq:estimate} holds true on $[0,t_0]$ We want to propagate this decay for all times, that is, we aim to show that $t_0=t_*$, which in turn implies that $t_0=t_*=T$, by \eqref{eq:O1}.
nodes.statement_short: The energy decreases initially, up to a maximal time $t_0$.

nodes.name: Coefficient control
nodes.statement: Let us emphasize that $\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)$ for $t\in [0,t_0]$ guarantees that \begin{equation} \Lambda_j(t)\leq \Lambda_j(0),\qquad j=1,2 \qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0]. \end{equation} Thereby, for any $t\in [0,t_0]$ we have that $$ \mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\geq \mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(0)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)=\gamma_1>0, $$ $$ \mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\geq \mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(0)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)=\gamma_2>0. $$ In particular, we obtain that \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)&< 0\qquad\mbox{for all}\quad t\in [0,t_0). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotone $\Lambda_j$ keeps the dissipation coefficients above $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$.

nodes.name: Contradiction on $t_0<t_*$
nodes.statement: Assume that $t_0<t_*$. By continuity, we deduce that $\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t_0)=\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(0)$, but this implies that, again, \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\bigg{|}_{t=t_0}&\leq 0, \end{align*} and that contradicts the assumption $t_0<t_*$.
nodes.statement_short: Assuming $t_0<t_*$ yields a contradiction.

nodes.name: Global smallness
nodes.statement: Thus, we have shown that in fact \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,t_*) \end{equation} and thereby $t_*=T$, in view of \eqref{eq:O1}.
nodes.statement_short: Hence the energy stays below its initial value and $t_*=T$.

nodes.name: Energy estimate
nodes.statement: Then, \begin{equation} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq -\gamma \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(t)\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\in[0,T), \end{equation} where $\delta:=\min\{\gamma_1,\gamma_2\}$. Eventually, the energy estimate for the gravity driven equation ($\mathcal S =0$) reads \[ \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+\delta\int_0^t \mathscr{E}^2_2(f,\Theta)(\tau)\, d\tau \leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0) \] and \[ \int_0^t \|\partial_t f(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\partial_t \Theta(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}\, d\tau\leq c, \] for all $t\in[0,T)$, where $c>0$ is a constant depending on the initial data.
nodes.statement_short: Integrated energy estimate and bound on time derivatives.

nodes.name: Fourier truncation
nodes.statement: We use a standard Galerkin approximation to obtain in the limit a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} where surface tension effects are neglected, \emph{i.~e.} $\mathcal{S}=0$. Let us fix $M\in {\mathbb Z}^+$. Set \[ f_M(t,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat f(t,k)e^{ikx}\qquad \mbox{and}\qquad \Theta_M(t,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat \theta(t,k)e^{ikx} \] and the initial data \[ f_M(0,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat f_0(k)e^{ikx}\qquad \mbox{and}\qquad \Theta_M(0,x):=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat \theta_0(k)e^{ikx} \] to coincide with the Fourier truncation of the $f_0$ and $\Theta_0$, respectively. Recall that the convergence of the Fourier series of the initial data is guaranteed by the assumption that $f_0,\Theta_0\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T})$.
nodes.statement_short: Define Fourier-truncated unknowns and initial data.

nodes.name: Truncated nonlinearities
nodes.statement: We consider the Galerkin approximated problems: \begin{alignat*}{2} \partial_t f_M-\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\partial_x^2 \Theta_M +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\partial_x^2 f_M+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\partial_x^4 f_M&=\sum_{j=1,2,4} N_j^M,\; && \text{ in }(0,T)\times{\mathbb T}\\ \partial_t \Theta_M -\left(h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\partial_x^2\Theta_M+\left(\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\right) \partial_x^2f_M+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2 \partial_x^4f_M &= \sum_{j=5,6,8} N_j^M,\;&& \text{ in }(0,T)\times{\mathbb T} \end{alignat*} where the nonlinearities $N_j^M$ are given by \begin{align*} N_1^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\left(\frac{f^2}{2}+fh_\sharp\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\ N_2^M&=\partial_x P_M \left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}\left(3h_\sharp^2 f+3f^2h_\sharp+f^3\right)\partial_x f\right],\\ N_4^M&=\mathcal{A} P_M \bigg{[}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp^2}\partial_x^2 f +\left(\frac{\partial_x f}{h_\sharp}\right)^2\right)\sum_{j=1}^M (-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}-\frac{f}{h_\sharp^3}(\partial_x f)^2\sum_{j=1}^M j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1} \bigg{]},\\ N_5^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\left(\Gamma_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp+\Theta f\right)\partial_x \Theta\right],\\ N_6^M&=\partial_x P_M\left[\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\left(\Gamma_\sharp f^2+2\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp f+\Theta h_\sharp^2+\Theta f^2+2\Theta h_\sharp f\right)\partial_x f\right],\\ N_8^M&=\frac{3\mathcal{A}}{2h_\sharp^4} P_M\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x^2 f+\left(2\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+2f\partial_x f\Gamma_\sharp-\partial_x \Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\partial_x f\right]\sum_{j=1}^M j(-1)^{j+1}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-1}\nonumber\\ &\quad- \frac{3\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp^4} P_M\left[\left(2f\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp+f^2\Gamma_\sharp-\Theta h_\sharp^2\right)\frac{(\partial_x f)^2}{h_\sharp}\right]\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j=2}^M j(j-1)(-1)^{j}\left(\frac{f}{h_\sharp}\right)^{j-2}. \end{align*} Here, the operator $P_M$ denotes the Fourier truncation operator \[ P_M g(x)=\sum_{|k|\leq M} \hat g(k)e^{ikx}\qquad\mbox{for any}\quad g\in \dot A^0({\mathbb T}). \]
nodes.statement_short: Truncated nonlinear terms via the projection $P_M$.

nodes.name: Global Galerkin solutions and uniform bounds
nodes.statement: The Picard--Lindel\"of Theorem ensures the existence of classical solutions \[ f_M,\Theta_M\in C^1([0,T_M);C^\infty({\mathbb T})), \] where $T_M>0$ is the maximal existence time. Furthermore, the approximated problems provide the same \emph{a priori} bounds as in the previous sections. Consequently the Galerkin solutions $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in {\mathbb N}}$ exist globally and for any $T>0$ we have the bounds: \begin{equation} (f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \quad \mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left( L^\infty\left(0,T;\dot A^0({\mathbb T})\right)\cap L^1\left(0,T; \dot A^2({\mathbb T}) \right)\right)^2 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} (\partial_t f_M,\partial_t\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \quad \mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left( L^1\left(0,T; \dot A^0({\mathbb T}) \right)\right)^2. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Picard-Lindelof plus a priori bounds give global approximations with uniform bounds.

nodes.name: Weak convergence
nodes.statement: Following the lines in \cite{BG18}, the above uniform regularities of the Galerkin approximations $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} $ guarantee the existence of a weakly convergent subsequences (not relabeled) such that \begin{align*} (f_M,\Theta_M)\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup} (f,\Theta)\text { in $\left(L^{\infty}(0,T;L^\infty({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$}. \end{align*} Similarly, using interpolation in Wiener spaces, the finite measure of the spatial domain and the fact that $\dot A^r({\mathbb T})\subset \dot W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T})$ for any $r\geq 0$, we obtain the existence of a subsequence (not relabeled), such that \begin{align} (f_M,\Theta_M)\rightharpoonup (f,\Theta)\text { in $\left(L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T;\dot W^{r,p}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$},\qquad 0\leq r<2,\;\;1\leq p<\infty. \end{align} From the previous fact we can infer that actually $$ (f,\Theta) \in \left(L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T;\dot W^{r,\infty}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2,\qquad 0\leq r<2. $$
nodes.statement_short: Extract weakly(-*) convergent subsequences.

nodes.name: $L^2H^1$ bound
nodes.statement: Furthermore \eqref{boundedness}, \eqref{boundednesst} imply that $$ (f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}} \text{ is uniformly bounded in } \left(L^2(0,T;H^{1}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2, $$ which is due to $\dot A^s({\mathbb T})\subset \dot H^s({\mathbb T})$ for any $s \geq 0$ and an interpolation inequality for fractional Sobolev spaces.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform $L^2H^1$ bound by embedding $\dot A^s\subset\dot H^s$.

nodes.name: Strong convergence
nodes.statement: Eventually, as a consequence of \eqref{boundedness},\eqref{boundednesst} and a compactness argument as in \cite[Corollary 4]{simon1986compact}, we obtain (up to a subsequence) that $$ (f_M,\Theta_M)\rightarrow (f,\Theta)\qquad \text{ in $\left(L^1(0,T;{C}^{1+s}({\mathbb T}))\right)^2$}, \quad \,0\leq s<\frac{1}{2}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Simon's compactness lemma gives strong convergence in $L^1C^{1+s}$.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit
nodes.statement: Passing to the limit in the weak formulation of the Galerkin approximation yields the existence of a global weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}.
nodes.statement_short: Limit is a global weak solution.

nodes.name: Dissipation inequality
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{eq:energyE} and the definition of $\delta>0$ in \eqref{delta}, we have that \begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq -\delta\mathscr{E}^2_2(f_M,\Theta_M)(t) \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Energy inequality for Galerkin approximations.

nodes.name: Exponential decay of approximations
nodes.statement: Using the Poincar\'e-like inequality \eqref{lem:P}, we also conclude that $$ \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq -\delta\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t) \qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0, $$ which in turn implies the exponential decay towards the equilibrium: \[ \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0. \]
nodes.statement_short: Poincare-like inequality gives exponential decay.

nodes.name: Pass decay to the limit
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{eq:Linf1} and the lower semi-continuity of the weak$-*$ convergence, we have that \begin{equation*} \|f(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}\leq \liminf_{k\to \infty}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower semicontinuity transfers the decay to the weak solution.

nodes.name: Sketch
nodes.statement: The proof follows a standard contradiction argument. For the sake of brevity, we only sketch the idea.
nodes.statement_short: Standard contradiction argument, only sketched.

nodes.name: Two solutions
nodes.statement: Assume that there exist two different solutions $(f_1,\Theta_1)$ and $(f_2,\Theta_2)$ starting from the same initial data $$ (f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A^0({\mathbb T})\right)^2. $$ Assume also that these solutions satisfy $$ (f_i,\Theta_i)\in \left( L^{1}(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2. $$
nodes.statement_short: Assume two distinct solutions with the same data and extra regularity.

nodes.name: Difference estimate
nodes.statement: Using the smallness of the initial data, the same estimates as in Subsection \ref{ss:e} yield that \begin{multline*} \frac{d}{dt}\left(\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\\ \leq C\left[\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right]\left(\|f_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|f_2\|_{\dot A^2}+\|\Theta_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^2}+1\right). \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Differential inequality for the difference.

nodes.name: Gronwall
nodes.statement: Now the statement is a consequence of Gronwall's inequality and the fact that $(f_1,\Theta_1)(0)=(f_2,\Theta_2)(0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Gronwall's inequality with zero initial difference.

nodes.name: Reduction to Section 4
nodes.statement: The proof essentially follows the arguments in the previous section, the main difference relying in the fact that for $\mathcal S>0$ we have that \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} is a system of mixed orders. Thereby the energy estimates require some additional investigation.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of Theorem 2: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}>0$
nodes.statement_short: Follow Section 4; mixed orders need extra estimates.

nodes.name: Local Galerkin solutions
nodes.statement: The existence of local solutions of the approximated Galerkin systems are straightforward due to Picard--Lindel\"of's theorem (see Subsection \ref{ss:gl}).
nodes.section: 5 Proof of Theorem 2: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}>0$
nodes.statement_short: Picard-Lindelof gives local Galerkin solutions.

nodes.name: Global existence via energy
nodes.statement: The energy estimates then ensure that the approximated solutions exist globally. Furthermore, the energy estimates provide the necessary a priori bounds to pass to the limit in the Galerkin approximation; thereby guaranteeing the existence of a global weak solution in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of Theorem 2: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}>0$
nodes.statement_short: Energy estimates give global approximations and the limit.

nodes.name: Inheritance of estimates
nodes.statement: In view of the weak lower semicontinuity of the norm, the global weak solution inherits the energy estimates for the approximated solutions and we can conclude the regularity and exponential decay of the solution.
nodes.section: 5 Proof of Theorem 2: Global existence and decay when $\mathcal{S}>0$
nodes.statement_short: Lower semicontinuity gives regularity and decay.

nodes.name: Local solution
nodes.statement: To perform our energy estimates let us assume that there exists a local solution $$ (f,\Theta)\in \left(C^1([0,T), \dot A^0({\mathbb T})) \right)^2 $$ of the fourth-order system \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} where $\mathcal{S}>0$, corresponding to initial data $(f_0,\Theta_0)$, satisfying \[ \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)<\min\{h_\sharp,\Gamma_\sharp\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Take a local solution with small initial energy.

nodes.name: Derivative of Wiener norms
nodes.statement: Similar as before, we have that \begin{align} \frac{d}{dt}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq\frac{h_\sharp^2}{2}\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2} +\left(\frac{\mathcal{A}}{h_\sharp}-\frac{\mathcal{G}}{3}h_\sharp^3\right)\| f\|_{\dot{A}^2} - \frac{\mathcal{S}}{3}h_\sharp^3\|f\|_{\dot A^4}+\sum_{j=1}^4\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0} ,\\ \frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq-\left(h_\sharp \Gamma_\sharp+\mathcal{D}\right)\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\left|\frac{3\mathcal{A}\Gamma_\sharp}{2h_\sharp^2}-\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp^2\frac{\mathcal{G}}{2}\right|\|f\|_{\dot A^2}+\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}h_\sharp^2\Gamma_\sharp\|f\|_{\dot A^4} +\sum_{j=5}^8\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on time derivatives including fourth-order terms.

nodes.name: Summation
nodes.statement: Keeping in mind the definitions of $\mathfrak{C_i}$, $i=1,2,3,$ in \eqref{constant1}, \eqref{constant2}, and \eqref{constant3}, we take the sum of the two inequalities above and obtain that $$ \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)+\mathfrak{C}_1\|f\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\mathfrak{C}_2\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}+\mathfrak{C}_3\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\leq \sum_{j=1}^8\|N_j\|_{\dot A^0}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Sum the two inequalities.

nodes.name: Reuse S=0 bounds
nodes.statement: Recalling \eqref{eq:energyE}, we have that \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}&\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)+\mathfrak{C}_3\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\\ &\leq \|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}+\|N_7\|_{\dot A^0} -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\Lambda_2(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}, \end{align*} where $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are defined in \eqref{eq:Lambda_1} and \eqref{eq:Lambda_2}, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Reuse the $\mathcal S=0$ estimates; only $N_3,N_7$ remain.

nodes.name: Bounds on N3, N7
nodes.statement: Thus we are left to estimate the remaining terms $\|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}$ and $\|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}$. Similarly as before, using the interpolation inequality in Wiener spaces, we estimate \begin{align*} \|N_3\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{19}{3}\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}, \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}&\leq \frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left(6\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{\dot A^0}+h_\sharp^2\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\\ &\quad +\frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left(8\Gamma_\sharp h_\sharp \|f\|_{A^1}+4\|\Theta\|_{A^1}h_\sharp^2\right)\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Interpolation bounds on $N_3$ and $N_7$.

nodes.name: Young's inequality
nodes.statement: Note that by Young's inequality, we have that $$ \|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}\leq \|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}^{\frac{1}{4}}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}^{\frac{3}{4}}\leq\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\left(\frac{1}{4\varepsilon}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\frac{3\varepsilon}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\right), $$ for any $\varepsilon>0$. In particular, as $\Theta$ and $f$ are nonzero (provided the initial data are nontrivial), we can take $$ \varepsilon=\frac{\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}}. $$ Thus, $$ \|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^3}\leq\frac{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^1}^2}{4\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}\|f\|_{\dot A^0}+\frac{3\mathscr{E}_0^0}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}\leq \frac{\|\Theta\|_{\dot{A}^2}\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{4}+\frac{3\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta)}{4}\|f\|_{\dot{A}^4}. $$ Then, we conclude that \[ \|N_7\|_{\dot A^0}\leq \frac{\mathcal{S}}{2}\left( (14h_\sharp\Gamma_\sharp +4h_\sharp^2)\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \|f\|_{\dot A^4}+h_\sharp^2\mathscr{E}_0^0(f,\Theta) \|\Theta\|_{\dot A^2}\right). \]
nodes.statement_short: Young's inequality with $\varepsilon=\mathscr E^0_0/\|\Theta\|_{\dot A^1}$ closes the $N_7$ bound.

nodes.name: Grouped energy inequality
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{eq:Lambda_3}, we can group terms as follows: \begin{align*} \frac{d}{dt}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)&\leq -\left(\mathfrak{C}_1-\Lambda_1(t)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}-\left(\mathfrak{C}_2-\left(\Lambda_2(t)+\frac{\mathcal{S}h_\sharp^2}{2}\right)\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|\Theta(t)\|_{\dot{A}^2}\\ &\quad-\left(\mathfrak{C}_3-\Lambda_3\mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\right)\|f(t)\|_{\dot{A}^4}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Energy inequality with three dissipation terms.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Repeating the argument from Section \ref{S:T1}, we conclude that \begin{equation} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t} \end{equation} where $\delta$ is defined in \eqref{delta}. The energy estimate for the capillary driven thin film ($\mathcal S >0$) reads \begin{equation*} \mathscr{E}^0_0(f,\Theta)(t)+ \int_0^t\delta \mathscr{E}^4_2(f,\Theta)(\tau)\, d\tau \leq \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_0,\Theta_0) \end{equation*} and \[ \int_0^t \|\partial_t f(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\partial_t \Theta(\tau)\|_{\dot A^0}\,d\tau \leq c, \] for all $t\in[0,T)$, where $c>0$ is a constant depending on the initial data.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity argument of Section 4 gives exponential decay and the energy estimate.

nodes.name: Global Galerkin approximations
nodes.statement: In a similar way as in Subsection \ref{ss:gl}, we obtain the existence of a sequence of global Galerkin approximations $(f_M,\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Global Galerkin approximations as in Section 4.2.

nodes.name: Uniform bounds
nodes.statement: Then, the energy estimates from above guarantee that for any $T>0$: $$ (f_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}\quad\mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad L^\infty(0,T; A^0({\mathbb T}))\cap L^1(0,T;A^4({\mathbb T}))\subset L^2(0,T;H^2({\mathbb T})) $$ and $$ (\Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}\quad\mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad L^\infty(0,T; A^0({\mathbb T}))\cap L^1(0,T;A^2({\mathbb T}))\subset L^2(0,T;H^1({\mathbb T})). $$ Moreover, the time derivatives satisfy $$ (\partial_t f_M,\partial_t \Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}\quad\mbox{is uniformly bounded in}\quad \left(L^1(0,T;A^0({\mathbb T}))\right)^2 $$ for any $T>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform bounds on $f_M$, $\Theta_M$ and time derivatives.

nodes.name: Convergences
nodes.statement: Consequently, we obtain the existence of a subsequence (not relabeled) such that \begin{align} \begin{split} &f_M\rightharpoonup f\text { in $L^{\frac{4}{s}}(0,T; W^{s,p}({\mathbb T}))$},\quad 0\leq s<4,\;\;1\leq p<\infty\\ &\Theta_M\rightharpoonup \Theta\text { in $L^{\frac{2}{r}}(0,T; W^{r,p}({\mathbb T}))$} ,\quad 0\leq r<2,\;\;1\leq p<\infty. \end{split} \end{align} Moreover, \begin{align*} f_M&\rightarrow f\qquad \text{ in $L^1(0,T;C^{3+\alpha}({\mathbb T}))$}, \quad \,0\leq \alpha<\frac{1}{2},\\ f_M&\rightharpoonup f\qquad \text{ in $L^2(0,T, H^2({\mathbb T}))$} \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \Theta_M&\rightarrow \Theta\qquad \text{ in $L^1(0,T;C^{1+\alpha}({\mathbb T}))$},\quad \,0\leq \alpha<\frac{1}{2},\\ \Theta_M&\rightharpoonup \Theta\qquad \text{ in $L^2(0,T, H^1({\mathbb T}))$}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Weak and strong convergence of a subsequence.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit
nodes.statement: Equipped with these convergences we can pass to the limit in the weak formulation and conclude the global existence of a weak solution of \eqref{eq:systemlinearized} for $\mathcal S>0$ in the sense of Definition \ref{defi1}.
nodes.statement_short: Limit is a global weak solution for $\mathcal S>0$.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: The proof follows the same ideas as in Subsection~\ref{ss:decay}.
nodes.statement_short: Same as Section 4.3.

nodes.name: Decay of approximations
nodes.statement: The sequence of Galerkin approximation $(f_M, \Theta_M)_{M\in{\mathbb N}}$ satisfies the energy estimates. In particular, we have the exponential decay towards the equilibrum in \eqref{eq:Es}: \[ \mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t}\qquad \mbox{for all}\quad t\geq0, \] where $\delta>0$ is defined in \eqref{delta}.
nodes.statement_short: Approximations decay exponentially by (41).

nodes.name: Pass to the limit
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{eq:Linf} and the lower semi-continuity of the weak$-*$ convergence, we have that \begin{equation*} \|f(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}+\|\Theta(t)\|_{L^\infty({\mathbb T})}\leq \liminf_{k\to \infty}\mathscr{E}^0_0(f_M,\Theta_M)(t)\leq \mathscr{E}_0^0(f_0,\Theta_0)e^{-\delta t} \end{equation*} for all $t\geq 0$, which proves the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Lower semicontinuity gives the decay for the limit.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Also the proof for the conditional uniqueness is similar to the one in Subsection \ref{ss:unique}.
nodes.statement_short: Same as Section 4.4.

nodes.name: Two solutions
nodes.statement: Assume that there exist two different solutions $(f_1,\Theta_1)$ and $(f_2,\Theta_2)$ starting from the same initial data $$ (f_0,\Theta_0)\in \left(\dot A({\mathbb T})\right)^2. $$ Moreover, we suppose that the solutions satisfy the additional regularity $$ (f_i,\Theta_i)\in \left( L^{1}(0,T;\dot A^4({\mathbb T}))\times L^1(0,T;\dot A^2({\mathbb T}))\right)^2 $$ for $i=1,2$.
nodes.statement_short: Two solutions with the same data and extra regularity.

nodes.name: Difference estimate
nodes.statement: Similar as for the energy estimate we compute that \begin{multline*} \frac{d}{dt}\left(\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right)\\ \leq C \left[\|f_1-f_2\|_{\dot A^0}+\|\Theta_1-\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^0}\right]\\ \times\left(\|f_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|f_2\|_{\dot A^2}+\|f_1\|_{\dot A^4}+\|f_2\|_{\dot A^4}+\|\Theta_1\|_{\dot A^2}+\|\Theta_2\|_{\dot A^2}\right). \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Differential inequality for the difference.

nodes.name: Gronwall
nodes.statement: Now the assertion follows by applying Gronwall's inequality and recalling that the solutions $(f_i,\Theta_i), i=1,2$ share the same initial data.
nodes.statement_short: Gronwall's inequality concludes.
